text:
Morgan: Heads up — seeing a small but reproducible latency spike on short-context requests after the latest kernel-autotune rollout (commit 0a9f3c). Dashboard: https://perf.redwood.local/dash/shortctx-spike :chart_with_upwards_trend: 
Alex: rough numbers? p95 / p99?
Morgan: p95 up ~12ms, p99 up ~28ms on our Ampere pool for seqlen <= 64. Throughput similar. Spike started right after autotune changed preferred kernel for short prefill from `matmul_vec16` -> `fused_attn_v2`
Ravi: do you have the autotune decision logs? sometimes the selector flips between kernels across steps and causes jitter.
Morgan: pasted selector log (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-15T10:02:11Z] request_id=rx1234 seq_len=32 model=redwood-3b chosen_kernel=fused_attn_v2 reason=latency_estimate
[2026-03-15T10:02:11Z] request_id=rx1234 step=decode chosen_kernel=matmul_vec16 reason=fallback_input_size_mismatch
[2026-03-15T10:02:11Z] request_id=rx1234 kv_state=warm kv_hits=low chosen_kernel=fused_attn_v2
```
Alex: looks like prefill picked fused but decode fell back to matmul. Handoff mismatch is expensive.
Sam: is this limited to prefill->decode transitions? we saw similar with other models where the path mismatch causes memory remaps.
Morgan: preliminary profiler flame snippet: `prefill: 9.8ms fused_attn_v2` `decode_step_1: 11.2ms matmul_vec16` `kernel_switch_cost: 6.4ms` -> adds up.
Ravi: KV cache warmup comment—if KV is cold, fused kernel has a different kv layout and decode forces conversion. That conversion cost can dominate for short contexts.
Lina: can we gate fused_attn_v2 for seqlen < 48 or require stable kv_hits before selecting it?
Alex: propose: add hysteresis on kernel selector: require same kernel chosen for prefill and first decode OR disallow fused if kv_hits < 0.7. Also add metric `kernel_handoff_rate` to detect.
Sam: simple reproducer: on dev harness run:
```
./perf_test --model redwood-3b --seq-len 32 --prefill 1 --decode-steps 16 --parallel 8
```
That reproduces the spike locally for me.
Morgan: confirmed with that repro. Running across Ampere and H100 to compare.
ci-bot: Canary deploy 0a9f3c -> infra/ampere completed with 12/12 instances. Monitoring enabled.
Ravi: quick mitigation: revert the autotune change for short-seq canary or add a forced-compat path that avoids conversion on first decode. Which is faster?
Morgan: revert is quickest; adding forced-compat needs kernel runtime change but preserves perf for long seq.
Lina: volunteer to run the revert canary and run the reproducer across both hw. Will post results.
Alex: also please collect `kv_hit_ratio` and `kernel_switch_count` per request in the next 30m window.
Morgan: creating an issue and canary rollback now. Issue: https://phabricator.redwood/ISSUE-2154. Checklist: revert canary -> run repro -> collect traces -> evaluate.
Sam: if revert fixes, we should implement selector hysteresis + kv threshold and re-roll.
Lina: preliminary results: on Ampere revert -> p95 back to baseline, p99 down to baseline+2ms. On H100 the original fused still okay (no conversion cost).
Ravi: suggests adding architecture-aware rule: allow fused_attn_v2 only on H100 or when kv_hits > 0.8 on Ampere.
Alex: agree. We'll need an autotune policy change: add (arch, seqlen, kv_hit) tuple to decision table. I'll draft policy PR.
Morgan: thanks all. Action items: Alex PR for policy, Lina run extended canary, Ravi validate kv metrics, Sam update reproducer script to log kernel_switch_count. I'll keep thread updated. :white_check_mark:
